elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: 14.2 "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer"; "Deliverable" is defined to include "other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer"

elements.element: Vendor assigns such deliverables/work product to Customer
elements.evidence: 14.2 "which Vendor hereby assigns to Customer" (present assignment)
14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; Vendor Technology = "Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation..."

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: 13.2 "embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer ... a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence"; 14.3 "To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: 14.1 "Customer owns all Customer Data ... No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services"
14.4 "No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; Deliverable excludes "generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel"

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business
elements.evidence: Customer now owns Deliverables outright (14.2), and 13.2 grants a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free ... licence to use ... modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business"

reasons: The single replacement to 14.2 flips Deliverable ownership to Customer with an express present assignment, completing the preferred position when read with the untouched 13.2 (embedded Vendor IP licence), 14.1 (Customer Data), 14.3 (Vendor pre-existing IP) and 14.4 (no joint ownership).

Edit is confined to the one offending sentence pair; the conforming second sentence removes the contradiction of a revocable, term-limited licence back to an owner rather than rewriting the clause. Deleting that sentence entirely would have been marginally tidier, but retaining it as a clarifying negative introduces no undefined term or dangling mechanic.

Unrelated commercial terms (Affiliate scope in 13.2, Vendor Technology identification and third-party material approval in 14.3, feedback mechanics in 14.4) remain effective; no Customer Data or IP assignment to Vendor is created.
